messages.body:
Dear Linnet Lane events team,

Thank you for coming to our community open day at the Westquay depot in September. The Hallbrook Community Fund trustees met on Tuesday 27 October to agree the autumn round, and I promised to let each partner charity know where things landed before the end of the month.

This round we received 41 applications against a pot of 18,000 pounds. The trustees have prioritised projects that keep people active and connected through the winter, and we have funded the Port Cressing lunch club, the Tidemouth young carers' trips and two community allotments. Your application for the bereavement walking group was not funded this time, but the trustees asked me to say it scored well and they would welcome it again in the spring round, which opens on 1 March.

Our volunteering days will continue into next year. If your shops or the hospice gardens could use a team of eight to ten colleagues for a day, please send me a few dates in February or March and I will put them to the depot managers.

Separately, under our matched giving scheme for colleagues: we will match the sponsorship raised by our colleague Dev Raghunathan (transport planner, Westquay) for his Kestrel Coast Marathon run for Linnet Lane Hospice, pound for pound up to the scheme limit of 300 pounds. His page has passed that, so the match is 300 pounds in full, and our payment of 300.00 pounds will reach your bank account by 6 November with the reference HCF-MG-2611. Please treat this email as our written confirmation of the match.

Finally, the fund's annual report will be published in January and will mention every partner charity; if you would like a different description of the hospice from last year's, let me know by 30 November.

With best wishes,

Eleri Vaughan-Price
Community Fund Coordinator
Hallbrook Logistics Ltd, Westquay Depot, Port Cressing
